result = yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point(remainder_re_ast, &re_ast, &remainder_re_ast, &min_gap, &max_gap); }","note":"The loop destroys the previous fragment and repeatedly splits the remainder, so a malformed chain can leave later processing operating on freed regexp nodes."},{"step":7,"file":"libyara/parser.c","function":"yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration","line":643,"var":"re_ast","code":"result = _yr_parser_write_string(identifier, string_flags, compiler, NULL, re_ast, &aux_string, ...)","note":"The freed-or-rewired AST fragment is then handed to string compilation, which traverses it again while building the rule string chain."},{"step":8,"file":"libyara/re.c","function":"yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point","line":456,"var":"re_ast","code":"int yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point(RE_AST* re_ast, RE_AST** result_re_ast, RE_AST** remainder_re_ast, int32_t* min_gap, int32_t* max_gap)","note":"The memory-safety sink is the AST-splitting routine itself, which dereferences and destroys nodes after the caller has already arranged overlapping ownership of the same tree."}]')
